title: The quiet corner
text: When the pupils at Willow School wanted a quiet place to read, they did not ask for a new building. They looked at an empty corner beside the library window. Three classes worked together to change it. One class collected cushions, another made book labels, and the oldest pupils painted a small shelf. The school caretaker helped them put it safely against the wall. At first, only storybooks were on the shelf. Then a pupil called Ben brought a book about trains. Soon there were books about animals, space and cooking too. The corner opens during lunchtime. Pupils may read there for fifteen minutes, so everyone gets a turn. They must put each book back before leaving. The head teacher says the best thing about the project is that the children planned it themselves.
items: They looked at an empty corner beside the library window.
Who helped put the shelf in place?
Ben brought a book about trains.
When can pupils use the corner?
Why are visits limited to fifteen minutes?

title: The missing lunchbox
text: On Tuesday, Max could not find his lunchbox. He remembered putting it on a bench after the morning football game. It was red and had a picture of a rocket. Max first looked in the classroom, but he only found his water bottle. His friend Sam suggested asking at the school office. The secretary had a blue lunchbox, but it was not Max's. Then Max saw a younger pupil carrying a red box across the playground. He was taking it to the office because he had found it under the bench. Max thanked him and checked inside. His sandwich and apple were still there. Nothing was missing. That evening, Max wrote his name inside the lid. He also decided to put his lunchbox straight into his bag after every meal.
items: Where did Max remember leaving his lunchbox?
He remembered putting it on a bench.
What did Max find in the classroom?
He only found his water bottle.
What colour was the box in the office?
The secretary had a blue lunchbox.
Why was the younger pupil carrying Max's box?
He was taking it to the office
He wanted to eat Max's lunch
He thought it was his own
He was taking it to the office.
What did Max do that evening?
He wrote his name inside the lid
Max wrote his name inside the lid.

title: A small weather station
text: Class Five decided to learn about the weather by making daily observations. They put a thermometer outside a north-facing window, away from direct sunlight. A clear container in the garden helped them measure rain. Every morning, two pupils checked the equipment and wrote the results in a notebook. The first week was dry, so there was no water to measure. Some children thought the container was broken. Their teacher explained that an empty container was also useful information. In the second week, heavy rain gave them plenty to record. At the end of the month, the class made a chart. They noticed that the wettest day was not the coldest one. The project did not help them predict every sunny day, but it taught them to look carefully and keep clear records.
items: They put a thermometer outside a north-facing window, away from direct sunlight.
How often did pupils record results?
Every morning, two pupils checked the equipment.
Why was the rain container empty in the first week?
The pupils emptied it too early
What did the final chart show?
The wettest day was not the coldest
Every wet day was very cold
The wettest day was not the coldest one.
What did the project teach the pupils?
To observe carefully and keep records
It taught them to look carefully and keep clear records.

title: The shoe-box theatre
text: During a wet weekend, Sara and her brother made a theatre from an old shoe box. They cut a large opening in the front and used a piece of blue cloth as a curtain. Sara drew the characters on card, and her brother fixed them to wooden sticks. Their story was about a little boat that wanted to reach an island. At first, the children wrote a very long story. When they practised, they forgot the words and knocked over the paper waves. They made the story shorter and gave each character only two lines. On Sunday evening, they invited their parents to watch. The show lasted five minutes. Their parents clapped, but the family cat slept through the whole performance. The children kept the box so they could make another play the following weekend.
items: What did the children use for the theatre?
They made a theatre from an old shoe box.
What was the curtain made from?
They used a piece of blue cloth as a curtain.
Why did they change the story?
They found the long version difficult to perform
They forgot the words and knocked over the paper waves.
How long was the final show?
What did the cat do during the show?
The family cat slept through the whole performance.

title: The community fridge
text: Near Leo's school, a community centre has a special fridge. Local shops leave extra food there when it is still safe to eat. Visitors can take what they need without paying. Two adults check the dates and clean the shelves every day. Leo's class visited the centre to learn how the project works. The children were not allowed to bring food from home because the centre has clear rules about what it can accept. Instead, they designed signs explaining the opening times. Leo drew a clock, and his friend Amy wrote the words in large letters. The fridge opens at four in the afternoon, after the volunteers have checked everything. Before the visit, Leo thought the project was only about saving money. Now he knows it also helps reduce the amount of food that is thrown away.
items: Where does the fridge's food come from?
Local shops leave extra food there.
Who checks the food each day?
They designed signs explaining the opening times.
The fridge opens at four in the afternoon.
What did Leo learn about the project?
It only helps shops make money
It also helps reduce the amount of food that is thrown away.

title: A map for visitors
text: The town museum asked a group of pupils to make a map for young visitors. The old map showed every room, but its words were small and difficult to read. The pupils walked through the museum with a guide and chose six interesting stops. These included an old kitchen, a model ship and a collection of toys. They drew simple pictures for each stop and used arrows to show the route. They did not include the upstairs room because it was closed for repairs. Before printing the map, the pupils asked two younger children to try it. One arrow sent them towards the toilets instead of the toy room, so the designers changed it. The new map now stands beside the museum entrance. Visitors can take a copy for free and return it when they leave.
items: What was difficult about the old map?
Its words were small and difficult to read.
How many stops did the pupils choose?
Why was the upstairs room left out?
It was too close to the entrance
The pupils asked two younger children to try it.
The pupils removed all the pictures
One arrow ... so the designers changed it.

title: The long journey of a seed
text: In spring, Olivia planted a bean in a clear cup beside the classroom window. She put wet paper around it so she could see the first root. Every day, she drew what had changed. For three days, nothing seemed to happen. Olivia wanted to throw the bean away, but her teacher asked her to wait. On the fourth day, a small root appeared. Soon a green shoot grew upwards. When the plant became too tall for the cup, Olivia moved it into a pot of soil. During the holidays, she took it home and put it on the balcony. Her brother helped her remember to water it. By the end of summer, the plant had produced several beans. Olivia saved two for next year's class and cooked the rest with her family.
items: Why did Olivia use a clear cup?
To keep the bean in darkness
She could see the first root.
When did a root first appear?
On the fourth day, a small root appeared.
Why did she move the plant into a pot?
It became too tall for the cup
The plant became too tall for the cup.
Where did the plant spend the holidays?
She took it home and put it on the balcony.
What did Olivia save for the next class?
Olivia saved two for next year's class.

title: The friendly football match
text: Two classes arranged a football match on the last Friday of term. At first, each class wanted only its fastest players on the team. Their sports teacher suggested a different plan: everyone who wanted to play should have a turn. The match was divided into short periods, and the teams changed players after each one. A pupil called Amir had never played in a school match before. He was worried about making a mistake, but his classmates encouraged him. Near the end, Amir passed the ball to a teammate, who scored. The final score was three goals each. Nobody received a special prize. Instead, the teacher gave both classes a certificate for working together. Amir was pleased that he had helped his team, and he decided to practise again the following week.
items: On the last Friday of term
On the first Monday of term
On the last Friday of term.
Giving every willing pupil a turn
Everyone who wanted to play should have a turn.
He was worried about making a mistake.
Amir's team won by three goals
The final score was three goals each.
Why did both classes get certificates?

title: The library cat poster
text: One morning, a small brown cat appeared outside the library. It was friendly and wore a blue collar, but there was no name on it. The librarian gave it water and asked the local animal centre for advice. While an adult looked after the cat, two pupils made a poster. They drew the cat carefully and wrote the library's phone number underneath. They did not put their own phone numbers on it. The posters went in the library window and the nearby shop. That afternoon, a woman called the library. Her cat, Pepper, had been missing since breakfast. She described the white patch under his chin, which was not shown on the poster. When she arrived, Pepper ran towards her. The pupils were happy that their careful work had helped him return home.
items: What colour was the cat's collar?
Who did the librarian ask for advice?
She asked the local animal centre for advice.
Which phone number was on the poster?
They wrote the library's phone number.
How did the woman show she knew the cat?
She described a hidden white patch
She described the white patch ... not shown on the poster.
What did Pepper do when the woman arrived?

title: An afternoon without screens
text: For a class project, Maya's family tried spending one Saturday afternoon without screens. They put their phones and tablets in a drawer after lunch. Maya expected to feel bored because she usually watched videos at that time. Her father brought out an old board game, but they discovered that two pieces were missing. Maya's little brother found some buttons to use instead. After the game, they baked small cakes. The first tray stayed in the oven too long, so the cakes were rather dark. The second tray was much better. Later, they walked to the park and listened to a man playing the violin. At six o'clock, they opened the drawer again. Maya had enjoyed the afternoon, especially making the cakes, and suggested trying another screen-free afternoon the next month.
items: Where did the family put their devices?
They put their phones and tablets in a drawer.
How did they replace the missing game pieces?
Her brother found some buttons to use instead.
Why were the first cakes dark?
They stayed in the oven too long
The first tray stayed in the oven too long.
What instrument did they hear in the park?

title: A useful mistake
text: Noah was making invitations for the school cooking club. He carefully wrote the date and place, but he forgot to add the starting time. On the morning of the first meeting, three pupils asked him when they should arrive. Noah felt embarrassed. He told his teacher that the invitations were no good and wanted to throw them away. The teacher showed him a way to fix them. They printed small strips with the time and stuck one on each invitation. Then they put a large reminder on the classroom door. The meeting began at half past three, and everyone arrived on time. The club made fruit sandwiches and talked about kitchen safety. For the next invitation, Noah made a checklist: what, where, when and what to bring. He kept it beside the computer.
items: He forgot to add the starting time.
They printed small strips with the time.
Where was a large reminder put?
They put a large reminder on the classroom door.
The meeting began at half past three.
What did Noah make for future invitations?

title: The train that waited
text: At the small station, a model railway club was preparing an exhibition. The trains were tiny, but the people who built the tracks took their work seriously. Twelve-year-old Finn had made a station from card. He wanted his model train to stop beside it, but the train always went too far. Finn first thought the track was too smooth. His aunt, who belonged to the club, suggested checking the speed. When Finn slowed the train down, it stopped in the right place. For the exhibition, he added a little sign showing the station's name. Visitors enjoyed watching the train arrive, wait and leave again. Finn was asked to explain his model to a group of younger children. He found speaking to visitors more difficult than building, but he felt more confident by the end of the day.
items: What had Finn made from card?
A bridge over a real river
Finn had made a station from card.
What was the problem with his train?
It went too far before stopping
The train always went too far.
When Finn slowed the train down, it stopped in the right place.
What did Finn add for the exhibition?
A sign with the station's name
A little sign showing the station's name.
What was harder for Finn than building?
He found speaking to visitors more difficult than building.

title: The winter coat collection
text: When cold weather arrived, the youth centre organised a coat collection. Families could bring clean coats that no longer fitted them. Volunteers checked the zips and buttons before putting the coats on rails. A sign asked people not to leave wet or damaged clothes. Twelve pupils helped after school on Wednesday. They sorted coats by size and made colourful labels. A pupil called Aisha found a tiny toy car in one pocket. Instead of keeping it, she gave it to the organiser, who put it in a lost-property box. On Saturday, families came to choose coats without paying. Some visitors also brought clothes to share. Aisha noticed that the project was not only about giving things away. It was also about making people feel welcome and helping useful clothes last longer.
items: What kind of coats could families bring?
Clean coats that no longer fitted
Clean coats that no longer fitted them.
Volunteers checked the zips and buttons.
How did the pupils sort the coats?
What did Aisha do with the toy car?
She gave it to the organiser
She gave it to the organiser.
What did families pay for a coat?
Families came to choose coats without paying.

title: The path beside the pond
text: A path beside the village pond had become difficult to use. In wet weather, people stepped around the muddy places and damaged the grass. The village council asked residents for ideas. Some wanted to cover the whole area with concrete, but others wanted to protect the plants. A local builder suggested a narrow wooden path raised slightly above the ground. Before work began, a wildlife expert checked where animals lived around the pond. The builders changed one part of their plan to leave a quiet corner undisturbed. After the path opened, a school class made signs asking visitors to stay on it and take their rubbish home. The new path is not a place for cycling fast. It is a place to walk slowly, watch the water and enjoy the pond without harming its edges.
items: Why was the grass being damaged?
People stepped around the muddy places and damaged the grass.
A local builder suggested a narrow wooden path.
Who checked the animals' living places?
A wildlife expert checked where animals lived.
What did the school class make?
What is the path intended for?
Walking slowly and watching the pond
It is a place to walk slowly, watch the water and enjoy the pond.

title: A different school lunch
text: For one week, the school kitchen asked pupils to help plan a new lunch menu. Each class suggested a dish, but every dish had to include vegetables. Class Five chose vegetable pasta. Before the kitchen cooked it for everyone, six pupils tasted a small amount and gave comments. Most liked the sauce, but two said the pieces of carrot were too large. The cook cut them smaller for the next test. On Friday, the new pasta was served with salad and bread. Pupils could choose fruit for dessert. The kitchen counted how much food was left on the plates and compared it with an ordinary Friday. There was less waste than usual. The cook said that listening to pupils had helped, although the kitchen could not serve everyone's favourite meal every day.
items: What did every suggested dish need to include?
Every dish had to include vegetables.
How many pupils first tasted the pasta?
Six pupils tasted a small amount.
What did the cook change after the first test?
The size of the carrot pieces
What could pupils choose for dessert?
Pupils could choose fruit for dessert.
What happened to food waste on Friday?
There was less waste than usual.

title: The sound walk
text: Instead of taking photographs on their class walk, the pupils were asked to listen. Their teacher called it a sound walk. They carried notebooks and stopped at five places around the school. At the gate, they heard buses and bicycle bells. Beside the sports field, they heard birds and a dog barking in the distance. The quietest place was not the library garden, as many pupils expected. A machine was cutting the grass there. The little courtyard behind the art room was quieter. Back in class, the pupils made a sound map. They used different symbols for natural sounds and sounds made by people. They did not record private conversations. The teacher wanted them to notice their surroundings, not listen to other people's business. Several pupils said they would pay more attention on their walk home.
items: How many places did they stop at?
Why was the library garden noisy?
A machine was cutting the grass
A machine was cutting the grass there.
The little courtyard behind the art room was quieter.
What did the pupils avoid recording?
They did not record private conversations.

title: The first chess lesson
text: When Arjun joined the chess club, he thought he needed to remember every rule immediately. His first partner was an older pupil called Jamie. Instead of beginning a full game, Jamie put only a few pieces on the board. He showed Arjun how each one moved and asked him to try short puzzles. Arjun mixed up the bishop and the rook several times. Jamie did not laugh; he showed the moves again. After three meetings, Arjun played his first complete game. He lost, but he understood why his king was in danger. The club teacher said this was useful progress. At home, Arjun made a small card with pictures of the pieces and their moves. He practised with his sister for ten minutes after dinner. By the next month, he was ready to help a new member learn.
items: His first partner was an older pupil called Jamie.
With a few pieces and short puzzles
By asking Arjun to read every rule
Jamie put only a few pieces on the board ... short puzzles.
How did Jamie react to mistakes?
What happened in Arjun's first complete game?
He lost but learnt from it
He lost, but he understood why his king was in danger.
Who practised with Arjun at home?

title: The repair cafe
text: At a monthly repair cafe, volunteers help people mend small household objects. There is tea and cake, but repairing things is the main activity. When Ella visited with her grandfather, they took a desk lamp that no longer worked. Only trained adults were allowed to check electrical items, so Ella watched from a safe distance. While the lamp was being checked, she joined a sewing table and learnt to replace a missing button. Her grandfather talked to a volunteer about his old radio. The lamp needed a new switch, which the volunteer could fit that afternoon. The radio required a part that was not available, so they took it home again. Ella learnt that not everything can be repaired immediately. She also discovered that a small repair can save an object from the rubbish bin.
items: How often is the repair cafe held?
What did Ella learn to do?
She learnt to replace a missing button.
What was wrong with the lamp?
The lamp needed a new switch.
Why did they take the radio home unrepaired?
The radio required a part that was not available.

title: The photo with no winner
text: The photography club displayed pictures of ordinary objects seen in unusual ways. One pupil photographed the shadow of a chair. Another took a close picture of an orange, so it looked like a small planet. The club leader asked visitors to write what each photograph made them think of. There was no vote for the best picture. Some pupils were disappointed because they wanted a winner. Then they read the visitors' comments. A photograph of an old key reminded one visitor of her grandmother's house. A picture of a puddle looked like a mountain lake to a younger child. The pupils discovered that people could see different stories in the same image. At the end, each photographer chose one interesting comment to keep beside their picture. The display stayed in the school entrance for a week.
items: Ordinary objects seen in unusual ways.
What looked like a small planet?
A close picture of an orange
An orange ... looked like a small planet.
What were visitors asked to do?
Write their thoughts about the pictures
Write what each photograph made them think of.
What did the old key remind one visitor of?
How long did the display stay at the entrance?

title: The welcome booklet
text: Before the new school year, Class Five made a booklet for younger pupils joining the school. They remembered how confusing their own first week had been. The booklet explained where to leave coats, how to borrow library books and whom to ask for help. The pupils used short sentences and drew pictures of important places. They wanted to include every school rule, but the teacher suggested choosing the most useful information first. A map on the middle pages showed the route from the entrance to the classrooms. Two new pupils tested the booklet during a summer visit. They found the classrooms easily but could not find the drinking-water tap. The class added a clear sign for it on the map. When school began, every new pupil received a copy, together with a friendly welcome from an older child.
items: Who was the booklet made for?
For younger pupils joining the school.
Why did the class want to help?
They remembered their own confusing first week
They remembered how confusing their own first week had been.
Choosing the most useful information first
Choosing the most useful information first.
What was difficult to find during the test?
They could not find the drinking-water tap.
What did each new pupil receive?
A booklet and a friendly welcome
A copy, together with a friendly welcome.
